summary: Do not ship. (1) R-1 is still open: the invariant at lines 174-175 contradicts its all-or-none intent and reverse fixtures. R-2 is resolved: lines 140-153 and 188-191 enforce strict scope through both adapters, lines 225-229 cover broad-scope and patch cases, and line 295 isolates the policy change in PR-C. (2) No separate new critical/high issue was found in the scope or PR-slicing fixes.
triage: review-gate SKILL.md rules govern: render EVERY finding as a full table row, the human decides each row (accept/reject/defer/question — free text), echo back before applying, max 2 rounds, append decisions.md and COMMIT it with this artifact.

findings.title: R-1 remains open because the biconditional permits partial states
findings.body: `S ⟺ (E ∧ K ∧ C)` is not an all-or-none invariant. For example, with S=false, E=true, K=false, and C=false, both sides evaluate false, so the biconditional passes—even though the reverse fixture at line 248 says this state must fail. An implementation following the stated formula therefore remains fail-open for most partial-removal combinations, retaining the stale-secret restart failure and dangling-reference risks from Round 1.
findings.recommendation: Replace the formula with explicit equality of all four facts, such as `(S && E && K && C) || (!S && !E && !K && !C)`, and require the gate tests to reject all 14 mixed truth-table states.

next_steps: Correct the R-1 invariant and align the gate description, implementation contract, and truth-table tests before shipping.
